entries.title: My folk are idle (standing around)
q: why are my villagers not working
entries.answer: Folk keep hours: night, the noon break, the rest day and festivals are time off. Otherwise an idle folk is short of something; ask it 'Your work today?'.
more: Outside those, an idle folk usually lacks something: the tool of its trade, materials in the stores for its building, food (a hungry folk can't work properly), or work in its trade (more hands than the trade needs).
steps: Check the time: it's work from the dawn bell (6:00) to the dusk bell (18:00), less the noon break.
Ask it 'Your work today?' (Chat → More chat) or 'How are you?': it says what it's doing or missing.
Press J: what the town is short of. Look at its Profile → Day (plan vs what it's really doing).
Feed the town (food in the stores), supply what its trade lacks, or sell the town materials.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → Your work today?
tips: Idle hands help the builders and bake bread, and the elder moves spare hands to trades that need them.
A folk with a red warning on its name tag is stuck: it digs or climbs its way out by itself.

Busy folk with a few minutes spare do chores, chat with a workmate, sit on the grass or drink at the well: that's their own time, not idleness. A hand with nothing to do is called to the town's waiting work first.

entries.title: Nobody buys from my shop
q: customers dont come to my shop
why do folk say too dear
entries.answer: Folk buy only what they need, at a fair price, while the shop is open. Open its screen: Getting started and Stock & prices say what to fix.
more: Check four things: is the shop open (every checklist line ticked, within its hours)?
Are its wares things folk here want (the Stock tab says who would buy each and why)?
Is its name good (fair prices, full shelves, a keeper who greets)?
steps: Open the shop → Shop tab: 'Getting started' shows what's missing, the next step first.
Stock & prices: read 'N of its wares have buyers in town' and 'Folk here want: ...'; stock those.
Press Going price on dear wares; 'too dear' turnings-down are on the Books tab.
Wait for hours: four customers a day at worst, two dozen at best; market day brings more.
warn: Worn tools don't sell; and nobody pays more than the town asks for something it has itself.

entries.title: My town isn't growing
q: why is my village not growing
how do i make my village bigger
my town isn't getting any bigger
entries.answer: A town grows only with free beds and food put by. Check the town's books Overview: food, homes and mood.
more: Children come only with room and food: a free bed (houses keep up with births) and a day's meals for everybody in the stores, from two fed folk in work.
So look at the larder, the homes and the mood; and the server's growth cap may stop a town past a size.
steps: Food short? Help the farms: bring food, deliver Wanted orders; the elder orders 'Fill the larder'.
Homes short? Builders need materials: bring planks, stone, glass.
Raise contentment: a thriving town needs less food put by and has children more readily.
controls: Town's books → Overview · People → Growth · Homes
warn: villageGrowthCap (100) and the world cap stop children past them: ask your server's operator.

entries.title: Nothing is getting built
q: why isnt my village building anything
why is the building taking so long
entries.answer: Builders use only what's in the stores, so a shortage means a wait. The town's books (Town, then Buildings) say what each is waiting for.
more: Some works also wait for an age, a hand the town can spare, or the town's own buildings first.
steps: Check what it waits for: the town's books → Town → Buildings, or your order on the property office's Orders tab.
Bring the material: sell it at the store, deliver it as a Wanted order, or give it to your order.
Paid orders get hands while fewer than half the town's grown folk are at its works.

entries.title: I can't found a town
q: why cant i found a town
entries.answer: The founding screen says why under Confirm: usually a server limit, no Founding Kit, or a spot too near another town.
more: Usually: the server only lets citizens or operators found; you've founded the most towns a player may (3 by default); you carry no Founding Kit, spawner or charter; or the spot is too near a town, in water, or out of reach.
steps: No kit? Craft one: 2 bread, wheat seeds, planks and a gold nugget.
Citizens only? Become a citizen of a town first ('May I live here?').
Pick another spot if this one is refused.

entries.title: The town won't make me a citizen
q: why cant i become a citizen
they wont let me live here
entries.answer: 'We hardly know you yet' means you're not a friend of the town yet. Talk with folk daily and give gifts; the U page shows your warmth (a friend at 12).
more: 'Not while you owe a fine' means pay it.
Otherwise it's 20 coins (unless the town built you a house).
steps: Talk to many folk daily; give presents; do errands.
Pay fines (Town → The watch → Pay a fine).
Carry 20 coins and ask 'Live here?' again.
controls: [U] → You and the town (your warmth: a friend at 12)

entries.title: The town won't charter my business
q: why cant i start a business
only a citizen or friend may hold a charter
say hello to the nearest folk
entries.answer: The town won't charter a business for a stranger. Say hello to a few folk first, or open a shop instead, which needs no standing.
more: The town charters anybody it knows and has nothing against: a citizen, a friend, or a visitor who has passed the time of day with its folk.
A stranger nobody has spoken to is told so on step 1 with a 'Say hello' button; an unwelcome player must mend fences first.
steps: Press 'Say hello to the nearest folk' on step 1 (or talk to a few folk).
Or open a shop instead: U → Open a shop.

entries.title: Folk are leaving my town
q: why are folk leaving my village
entries.answer: After three miserable days, folk start to leave. Lift the town's contentment: food, homes, wages and things to enjoy.
more: After three miserable days (contentment under 25) somebody leaves, one every other day at most and never below eight.
Folk also move for work a Wanted notice offers elsewhere, or when unhappy.
steps: Check the town's books → Overview: contentment and its parts.
Talk round one thinking of leaving: 'Won't you stay?'.

entries.title: My town is stuck in an age
q: my town is stuck in the stone age
why wont my village reach the iron age
not enough iron for the next age
how do i help my town advance
entries.answer: Each age needs things in the stores and buildings standing. Press J to see what's short, then bring it.
more: Press J for what the town is short of, then help: deliver the Wanted orders, sell it iron or stone, take its quests, or bring its errands ('Can I help?' asks for what the next age needs).
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Can I help?

entries.title: My items disappeared in town
q: lost my loot when i died in town
entries.answer: Things left lying in a town's streets go to its Lost and Found chest by the storehouse, kept for you for three days.
more: Ask the storekeeper 'Lost & found' or right-click the chest.

entries.title: The folk don't like me
q: why dont the folk like me
entries.answer: Something you did cost you their good opinion. Say sorry, pay what you owe and give gifts they like; grudges fade with time.
more: Something cost you: hitting a folk, a theft or broken building seen by a witness, a fine unpaid, a quest given up, a bribe found out, or hated gifts.
Say sorry (once a day each), pay what you owe, give liked presents, and let grudges fade; an outcast who stays away long enough can come back.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → I'm sorry
Town → The watch → Pay a fine

entries.title: The town's books are empty
q: the town's books are written each morning
entries.answer: The town's books are written each morning, so a new town's pages fill in from its first day.
more: Overview, Folk, Society, Leader and News have today's figures already.

entries.title: My business is in trouble
entries.answer: A new firm has a week's grace, and you're told each day what's wrong. Open Your businesses (U) and follow what it says.
more: If it owes more than it's worth or runs out of cash and credit, you're told once a day in chat, and Your businesses says what's wrong, what to do (coin in its till on the Money tab, stock, a hand) and how many days are left before creditors may take it to court.

entries.title: Nobody's near enough to ask
q: ask the nearest folk does nothing
u page button says find a folk
entries.answer: 'Ask the nearest folk' buttons need an awake, grown folk within about twelve blocks. Walk up to one and try again.

entries.title: The game is slow near a big town
entries.answer: Hundreds of folk are heavy for a computer. Found smaller towns and turn name tags down (K, then Name tags).
more: Every folk is a ticking creature and drawn with its own animations, so hundreds are heavy.
Found smaller towns; on your side, turn down how much of the folk's life is drawn (the client animation config) and name tags (K → Name tags).
Operators can cap growth and let far towns sleep.

entries.title: My town is hungry
q: not enough food in the village
entries.answer: A hungry town puts more hands on its farms by itself. You can help by bringing food: Wanted orders, errands or selling at the store.
more: A hungry town orders the larder filled: half as many farmers and fishers again, wider fields, and in a famine twice the farmers and bread bought from traders.

entries.title: A screen says it's opening
q: opening the town's books takes a while
nothing happens when i press u
the books take long to open
entries.answer: Screens that wait on the server (the town's books, your page, finances, the journal, a folk profile) show an 'Opening…' line at once; the screen follows when the server answers.
tips: If it never opens, you may be out of reach of any town: walk into one and try again.
